meta.description: Every kwarg litellm/_redis.py can pass to redis-py, by tested redis-py version, next to how SETTINGS in litellm-rust/crates/redis-resolve/src/keys.rs handles it
meta.method: uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with redis==<version> python -I, reading inspect.getfullargspec(inspect.unwrap(cls.__init__)) args and kwonlyargs, minus self

signatures.sync: redis.Redis.__init__. _get_redis_kwargs uses it as the config allowlist and the REDIS_<KWARG> environment mapping
signatures.async: redis.asyncio.Redis.__init__, which the proxy constructs. A kwarg in sync but not async raises TypeError when the client is built
signatures.connection: redis.Connection or redis.asyncio.Connection MRO, the url allowlist from _get_redis_url_kwargs

rust.supported: true when the Rust client honors the setting, which is only the Read rows

handling.Warn: dropped and returned as an Ignored warning naming the consequence
handling.Reject: fails with RedisError::Unenforceable when set to true
handling.unlisted: no SETTINGS row, so it lands in passthrough for a redis-py host and the Rust client never uses it, without a warning
handling.unlisted_host_object: no SETTINGS row and listed in HOST_OBJECTS, so it lands in host_objects and the Rust client never uses it, without a warning

rust.field: the Options field in litellm-rust/crates/redis-resolve/src/options.rs that a Read row fills, null otherwise

meta.versions: each entry is a redis-py version whose signatures name the arg, with which ones. An empty array means no signature names it, so it only reaches Python as a litellm key
